leads.summary: Real Kitty continuation lines survive the new rewrite, so the face or family still has the old tail
leads.consequence: At Kitty 0.49.1, a continuation is a NEXT physical line whose first non-space character is backslash. For `bold_font family="Old Font"` followed by `  \ style=Heavy`, one font-set produces `bold_font Test Font` followed by `  \ style=Heavy`; Kitty joins them into `bold_font Test Font style=Heavy`, not the bare selected family. The same mismatch applies to font_family and all three faces. The new test uses trailing-backslash syntax Kitty does not treat as a continuation, so its success and its failure against the previous head do not establish a fix for genuine continuations. An explicit auto line is left intact. Suggest detecting/consuming subsequent leading-backslash lines belonging to rewritten keys, according to Kitty's parser.

leads.summary: Trailing backslash on a rewritten Kitty font line destroys unrelated following settings
leads.consequence: Kitty does not continue a line merely because it ends in backslash. If `bold_font Old Font \` is followed by `font_size 22.0`, the new sed `N` joins that independent font_size directive to the face and the subsequent substitution deletes it. The font_family branch does the same, and repeated suffix-backslash lines can remove multiple independent directives (for example window_padding_width). The command exits 0 and signals Kitty, the user loses the settings on this and later runs, while the previous script retained them. With such a line at EOF, sed N also skips the replacement and leaves an old face. Only join lines that Kitty itself regards as continued; leave unrelated directives in place.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** At `e1106ff`, kitty's leading-`\` continuations still keep a stale tail, and the new trailing-`\` handling can delete the next line.

Since the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12171#issuecomment-5865750873), earlier findings and the Ghostty/foot note stay addressed.

### Kitty continuations keep their stale tail

kitty 0.49.1 appends a next line starting with `\`, so `bold_font family="Old Font"` + `\ style=Heavy` still reads as `Test Font style=Heavy`. The new test uses the trailing form.

**Suggested change:** instead of joining lines ending in `\`, drop following lines that start with `\` (after blanks), and test that form.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at e1106ff)</summary>

kitty 0.49.1 continues a setting when the *next* line starts with `\` after optional indentation (`kitty/conf/utils.py`, `_parse`, lines 397-408; the Go parser in `tools/config/api.go` lines 168-180 does the same). A `\` at the end of a line does not continue it. At `e1106ff` the new sed programs only join lines that *end* in `\`, so a real kitty continuation is left in place and kitty joins it onto the rewritten line.

Save as `test/shell.d/kitty-continuation-test.sh` and run `bash test/shell.d/kitty-continuation-test.sh` from the repository root.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail
source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/base-test.sh"

test_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_dir"' EXIT
test_home="$test_dir/home"
kitty_config="$test_home/.config/kitty/kitty.conf"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$kitty_config")" "$test_dir/bin"

# Exercise the real font command without changing the running desktop.
for command in pkill omarchy-restart-shell omarchy-hook omarchy-notification-send; do
  printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' >"$test_dir/bin/$command"
done
printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 1\n' >"$test_dir/bin/pgrep"
printf '#!/bin/bash\nprintf "Test Font\\n"\n' >"$test_dir/bin/fc-list"
printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' >"$test_dir/bin/kitty"
chmod +x "$test_dir/bin/"*

run_command() {
  env HOME="$test_home" OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" PATH="$test_dir/bin:$ROOT/bin:$PATH" "$ROOT/bin/$@"
}

# kitty continues a setting on the next line when that line starts with a
# backslash, after optional indentation (kitty/conf/utils.py, _parse).
cat >"$kitty_config" <<'CONF'
font_family Old
\ Font
bold_font family="Old Font"
    \ style=Heavy
bold_italic_font Old Font
\ style=Bold
\ extra=Tail
# italic_font Manual Edit
\ not-a-face
font_size 13
CONF
run_command omarchy-font-set 'Test Font'
grep -qx 'font_family Test Font' "$kitty_config" || fail "font command rewrites a continued family line"
grep -qx 'bold_font Test Font' "$kitty_config" || fail "font command rewrites a continued face line"
grep -qx 'bold_italic_font Test Font' "$kitty_config" || fail "font command rewrites a multi-line face"
! grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*\\ (Font|style=|extra=)' "$kitty_config" || fail "no kitty continuation tail survives a font change"
grep -qx '\\ not-a-face' "$kitty_config" || fail "font command leaves a commented line's continuation alone"
grep -qx 'font_size 13' "$kitty_config" || fail "font command keeps unrelated settings"
pass "font command drops kitty continuation lines of rewritten font lines"
```

Actual output at `e1106ff` (exit status 1):

```text
not ok - no kitty continuation tail survives a font change
```

The same test fails at `d8bbd1d` (the script before the continuation commits) with the same message, so `942abb0` did not change this case.

Actual `kitty.conf` before and after one `omarchy font set 'Test Font'` at `e1106ff`, with the settings that kitty 0.49.1's `_parse` and `parse_line` functions produce from each file (the functions were extracted from kitty's source and run on their own; kitty itself was not run):

```text
before                              after
font_family Old Font                font_family Test Font
bold_font family="Old Font"         bold_font Test Font
\ style=Heavy                       \ style=Heavy
font_size 13                        font_size 13

kitty reads bold_font as:
  family="Old Font" style=Heavy       Test Font style=Heavy
```
</details>

### Next line deleted after a trailing `\`

A rewritten font line ending in `\` now deletes the next line (e.g. `font_size 13`), a separate setting; at end of file it is not rewritten. Rare, but new.

**Suggested change:** the change above covers this.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at e1106ff)</summary>

Because the new sed programs treat a trailing `\` as a continuation, the line after a rewritten `font_family`, `bold_font`, `italic_font` or `bold_italic_font` line that ends in `\` is joined and then discarded, even though kitty reads that line as a separate setting. At the end of the file the same `\` line is not rewritten at all.

Save as `test/shell.d/kitty-trailing-backslash-test.sh` and run `bash test/shell.d/kitty-trailing-backslash-test.sh` from the repository root.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail
source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/base-test.sh"

test_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_dir"' EXIT
test_home="$test_dir/home"
kitty_config="$test_home/.config/kitty/kitty.conf"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$kitty_config")" "$test_dir/bin"

# Exercise the real font command without changing the running desktop.
for command in pkill omarchy-restart-shell omarchy-hook omarchy-notification-send; do
  printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' >"$test_dir/bin/$command"
done
printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 1\n' >"$test_dir/bin/pgrep"
printf '#!/bin/bash\nprintf "Test Font\\n"\n' >"$test_dir/bin/fc-list"
printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' >"$test_dir/bin/kitty"
chmod +x "$test_dir/bin/"*

run_command() {
  env HOME="$test_home" OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" PATH="$test_dir/bin:$ROOT/bin:$PATH" "$ROOT/bin/$@"
}

# A trailing backslash does not continue a kitty setting, so the next line is
# a setting of its own and must survive.
cat >"$kitty_config" <<'CONF'
bold_font Old Font \
font_size 13
CONF
run_command omarchy-font-set 'Test Font'
grep -qx 'font_size 13' "$kitty_config" || fail "font command keeps the setting after a trailing backslash"
pass "font command keeps the line after a trailing backslash"
```

Actual output at `e1106ff` (exit status 1):

```text
not ok - font command keeps the setting after a trailing backslash
```

The same test passes at `d8bbd1d` and at the base `b18ab49`.

Actual `kitty.conf` before and after one `omarchy font set 'Test Font'`:

```text
before                  after at d8bbd1d          after at e1106ff
font_family Old Font    font_family Test Font     font_family Test Font
bold_font Old Font \    bold_font Test Font       bold_font Test Font
font_size 13            font_size 13              (deleted)

before                  after at d8bbd1d          after at e1106ff
font_size 13            font_size 13              font_size 13
font_family Old Font \  font_family Test Font     font_family Old Font \   (not rewritten)
```
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**kitty source:** `kitty/conf/utils.py` `_parse` (v0.49.1) strips the next line's leading whitespace and appends it while it starts with `\`; the Go parser in `tools/config/api.go` does the same. A trailing `\` is not a continuation; for a font setting kitty then rejects the value (`Trailing backslash at end of input data`) and reports the line as a bad config line (from source; kitty was not run).

**Candidate fix** (tested in the sandbox: both reproducers pass, and the PR's earlier test cases still pass; the PR's trailing-`\` test block would need the kitty form):

```diff
--- a/bin/omarchy-font-set
+++ b/bin/omarchy-font-set
@@ -38,10 +38,11 @@
     # stale tail, which kitty joins onto the new family. Drop continuation
     # lines whenever this key line is rewritten.
     sed --follow-symlinks -i -E \
-      -e '/^[[:space:]]*font_family([[:space:]]|$)/{' \
-      -e ':join' \
-      -e '/\\$/{N;s/\\\n[[:space:]]*//;b join}' \
-      -e 's/^[[:space:]]*font_family[[:space:]]+.*/font_family '"$kitty_font_name"'/' \
+      -e '/^[[:space:]]*font_family[[:space:]]/{' \
+      -e 's/^[[:space:]]*font_family[[:space:]].*/font_family '"$kitty_font_name"'/' \
+      -e ':join' -e '$b' -e 'N' \
+      -e '/\n[[:space:]]*\\[^\n]*$/{' -e 's/\n[^\n]*$//' -e 'b join' -e '}' \
+      -e 'P' -e 'D' \
       -e '}' ~/.config/kitty/kitty.conf
   else
     printf '\nfont_family %s\n' "$font_name" >>~/.config/kitty/kitty.conf
@@ -55,11 +56,12 @@
   # font_family above, drop backslash continuations of rewritten face lines.
   for face in bold_font italic_font bold_italic_font; do
     sed --follow-symlinks -i -E \
-      -e '/^[[:space:]]*'"$face"'([[:space:]]|$)/{' \
+      -e '/^[[:space:]]*'"$face"'[[:space:]]/{' \
       -e '/^[[:space:]]*'"$face"'[[:space:]]+auto([[:space:]]|$)/b' \
-      -e ':join' \
-      -e '/\\$/{N;s/\\\n[[:space:]]*//;b join}' \
-      -e 's/^[[:space:]]*'"$face"'[[:space:]]+.*/'"$face $kitty_font_name"'/' \
+      -e 's/^[[:space:]]*'"$face"'[[:space:]].*/'"$face $kitty_font_name"'/' \
+      -e ':join' -e '$b' -e 'N' \
+      -e '/\n[[:space:]]*\\[^\n]*$/{' -e 's/\n[^\n]*$//' -e 'b join' -e '}' \
+      -e 'P' -e 'D' \
       -e '}' ~/.config/kitty/kitty.conf
   done
   pkill -USR1 kitty
```

**Verified at `e1106ff`:**
- Faces sync on the first font set with `font_family` commented out (earlier finding still resolved).
- `auto`, commented and absent face lines, including their `\` continuations, are left unchanged.
- Keys sharing a prefix (`bold_font_x`, `font_features`), a symlinked `kitty.conf` and sed metacharacters in the name are handled; a second identical run changes nothing.
- The new test fails with the previous script (`not ok - no continuation tail survives a font change`) and passes at the head.

**Related open PRs:** #13235 merged cleanly with the previous script but now conflicts in `bin/omarchy-font-set`, because the `font_family` sed line it adds its face loop after was rewritten. #9168 still conflicts.

**Pre-existing, not covered by either version:** a face key whose whole value is on a continuation line (`bold_font` then `\ Old Font`) stays stale, in the PR and in the fix above.
</details>
